decision_conditions: It has not been demonstrated that the proposal would comply with Condition A.3 (a) similar facing materials) of Class A, Part 1, Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended).

It has not been demonstrated that the proposal would comply with  'Condition  A.1 (j) (i) the enlarged part of the dwellinghouse would extend beyond a wall forming a side elevation of the original dwellinghouse and exceed 4 metres in height of Class A, Part 1, Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended).

It has not been demonstrated that the proposal would comply with  Condition B.2 (b)  (ii) other than in the case of an enlargement which joins the original roof to the roof of a rear or side extension, no part of the enlargement extends beyond the outside face of any external wall  (side or rear) of the original dwellinghouse of  Class B, Part 1, Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended).

The application was not accompanied by a technical report demonstrating that the proposed air source heat pump complies with MCS Planning Standards. Therefore, it has not been confirmed that the proposal would comply with Class G.1.Part 1, Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended).

In the context of Section 55 (2) (a) (ii)  Officers are of the opinion that the proposed external insulation render is to be applied to the proposed sides, rear and elements of the front elevations of the dwelling only.  On this basis, it is considered that the proposed external wall insulation would materially affect the external appearance of the building and as such the proposed external insulation is considered to comprise development which would require planning permission.
